info.title: Skald API
info.description: A server has two addresses. `<public URL>`, the server setting `--public-url`, is where the CLI and devices reach it. `<web URL>`, the setting `--web-url`, by default the public URL, is where browsers sign in: the providers' callbacks, the pages a sign-in returns to, its cookies, the `Origin` its browser forms are taken from and the verification page.

delete.description: Deletes the session's account, never while a space blocks it, as `GET /account/deletion` gives them: of a deletion and a revision at once that would leave such a space, one is refused. At once, on every instance: every session of the account ends, its WebSocket connections closing with the reason `account-deleted`; its service devices' tokens, its link runs and its approved device codes end; its sign-in methods are removed, so a method's next sign-in signs up as a new account, or is refused under the server's sign-up policy; its username is free; each of its devices is served as a revoked one, with `account-deleted` for devices with server-held certificates asking for a session by key, and no wrap to its recovery key or browsers is kept; each space `deletes` lists is deleted with its channels, history and tokens. Each space with other members keeps the account in its revisions and still gives its devices' certificates and revocations, marks it deleted in `GET /spaces/{space}/members` and `GET /spaces/{space}/devices`, and its members' devices get a `space-notice`. Nothing undoes a deletion. Only with a device session's bearer token, or a web session's cookie from a page of the web URL, whose sign-in is more recent than the server setting `--link-sign-in-age`; never with a service token.

400.description: The server refuses the stated version.

401.description: The request has no session, or an unknown, ended or expired one, or an `Authorization` header that is not `Bearer <token>` of a device session, such as a service token's.

403.description: Nothing is deleted. The problem `https://skald.so/problems/not-allowed`: a web session's request does not come from a page of the web URL. The problem `https://skald.so/problems/sign-in-too-old`: the session's sign-in is older than `--link-sign-in-age`; the person signs in again first.

409.description: Nothing is deleted. The problem `https://skald.so/problems/deletion-blocked`: the spaces that block the deletion.

The server does not check the anchors.

post.description: The new device's hello opens a run of CPace keyed by its link code (docs/protocol/membership.md, "Link code"): the server relays it between sessions of the account and never sees the code. The hello names a device of the session's account registered without a certificate, and replaces that device's open run, whose messages are then refused. The run ends on a `link-abort` from either side, once its device has a certificate, and when its code expires: the server setting `--link-code-lifetime` after the hello, 5 minutes unset.

The first account whose session enters a pairing pairs the run; the same account entering it again gets the hello again. An account enters at most 10 pairings the server does not hold within 15 minutes.

post.description: A device of the session's account stores a revocation of one of the account's devices (docs/protocol/membership.md, "Revocation"), as the bytes the server got. The server stores it only if it counts against the account's master key, the certificates the server holds and the revocations it stored before. Once stored, each device that checks 3 and 4 of "Device checks" revoke with the account's revocations has no certificate wherever the server checks one: its mailbox entries expire, its KeyPackages are deleted, its connections close and it gets no later entry.

A web session's links in progress end with it. A device session's device, its keys and its certificate stay, as at `DELETE /session`. delete.summary: Remove a sign-in method of the account
delete.description: Removes a sign-in method of the web session's account, never its last one: of two removals at once that would leave none, one is refused. The web sessions it signed in end at once, as at `DELETE /account/sessions/{session}`; device sessions stay. The removed method reaches no account: its next sign-in signs up as a new account, or is refused under the server's sign-up policy, and another account may link it. Only with a web session's cookie, from a page of the web URL, and a sign-in more recent than the server setting `--link-sign-in-age`: anything else removes nothing.

post.description: Device authorization (RFC 8628, §3.1): when at least one sign-in provider is configured, a machine without a browser asks for a device code and a user code. Its person approves the user code on the verification page, `GET /device`, within `expires_in` seconds, the server setting `--device-code-lifetime`; the machine meanwhile polls `POST /auth/token` every `interval` seconds, the server setting `--device-poll-interval`.

200.description: A new device code and its user code.

400.description: The server refuses the stated version (`application/problem+json`), or the request (`application/json`, RFC 6749, §5.2): `invalid_request` without a `client_id` or with one twice, `invalid_client` with another `client_id`.

404.description: Sign-in is off: the server has no sign-in settings.

put.summary: Attach an invite proof to a device sign-in
put.description: The machine calls this before it opens the verification page. While sign-up is closed, a proof that verifies with the invite's key is attached to its pending device authorization. If the server's sign-up policy would refuse the identity, sign-in from that authorization creates an account only if the invite is still held, live and unused. The invite then belongs to that account. If sign-in is already allowed, it leaves the invite available.

204.description: The request is well formed. The response reveals nothing about the authorization, invite or proof.

400.description: The server refuses the stated version or the request body is malformed.

404.description: Sign-in is off: the server has no sign-in settings.

get.description: Opened by the browser. Sends it to GitHub's authorization page, asking for no scope, with a `state` that the cookie this response sets binds to this browser and an S256 PKCE challenge of this sign-in. The `state` works once, until it expires; its lifetime is the server setting `--sign-in-state-lifetime`.

parameters.name: return_to
parameters.description: The page of the web URL to return to once signed in: a path such as `/settings?tab=devices`, or its full address. Anything else, such as another site's address or the public URL's, returns to `/` of the web URL.

Location.description: GitHub's authorization page with the app's client ID, the callback `<web URL>/auth/github/callback`, `state`, `code_challenge` and `code_challenge_method=S256`.

Set-Cookie.description: The cookie that binds `state` to this browser: `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Secure` under an https web URL, for the callback's path only.

404.description: GitHub sign-in is off: the server has no GitHub settings.

get.description: Opened by the browser on its way back from GitHub. Checks `state` against the browser's cookie, exchanges `code` with the app's client ID and secret and the sign-in's PKCE verifier and reads the GitHub user. The first sign-in of a GitHub user creates an account with the user's GitHub ID as its GitHub sign-in method; later ones reach the account that holds that method and update the method's GitHub login. While the server's sign-up is closed, a first sign-in creates an account for a GitHub login on the server's list, compared without case, or through `PUT /auth/device/invite`; the GitHub user's email does not count. Keeps no GitHub token. For a link, started by `POST /auth/github/link`, it adds the GitHub sign-in method to the account of the web session that started the link instead of signing in.

parameters.description: The code GitHub gives.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: The `state` of the sign-in start.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: GitHub's error, such as `access_denied`, instead of a code.

200.description: Signed in or linked: a page that sends the browser to the return page. For a link whose request lacks the cookie of the web session that started it, as one from another site lacks the `SameSite=Strict` cookie, first, once, a page that opens this callback again from this server.

Set-Cookie.description: Signed in: the session cookie `skald_session`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Secure` under an https web URL; signed in or linked: the removal of the cookie that bound `state`.

400.description: No one is signed in, or nothing is linked: `state` is missing, wrong, from another browser, expired or used, also by the end of the web session that started a link, or GitHub gave no code or refused it.

403.description: A link that links nothing: the browser is not under the web session that started it, or that session ended during the callback. Or a refused sign-up: the server's sign-up is closed and the person, who has no account, is on none of its lists and has no usable invite proof on the device authorization; the page names the problem type `https://skald.so/problems/sign-up-closed`, and nothing is created. A sign-in from the verification page with a user code refuses that code too: its polls answer `sign_up_closed`.

404.description: GitHub sign-in is off: the server has no GitHub settings.

409.description: A link that links nothing: another account has this GitHub sign-in method. Accounts never merge or move a method.

500.description: No one is signed in, or nothing is linked: the database failed.

502.description: No one is signed in, or nothing is linked: GitHub failed or refused the app's client ID and secret.

post.summary: Start a link of a GitHub sign-in method
post.description: Submitted by a form of a page of the web URL, such as `GET /sign-in-methods`, with the web session's cookie: a request whose `Origin` is any other, or that has none, links nothing. The web session's sign-in has to be more recent than the server setting `--link-sign-in-age`. Sends the browser to GitHub as `GET /auth/github` does, with a `state` that also binds the link to this web session; GitHub comes back through `GET /auth/github/callback`. The link works only while the session lasts.

parameters.name: return_to
parameters.description: The page of the web URL the link returns to, as `return_to` of `GET /auth/github` names it; by default `GET /sign-in-methods`. Anything else, such as another site's address, returns to `/` of the web URL.

Location.description: GitHub's authorization page, as `GET /auth/github` sends the browser to.

Set-Cookie.description: The cookie that binds `state` to this browser, as `GET /auth/github` sets it.

403.description: Nothing is linked: the request has no web session, comes from another site, or its session's sign-in is older than `--link-sign-in-age`: then a page that asks to sign in again.

404.description: GitHub sign-in is off: the server has no GitHub settings.

get.description: Opened by the browser. Sends it to Google's authorization endpoint, by OpenID Connect's authorization code flow, asking for the scopes `openid` and `email` only, with a `state` that the cookie this response sets binds to this browser and a `nonce` and an S256 PKCE challenge of this sign-in. The `state` works once, until it expires; its lifetime is the server setting `--sign-in-state-lifetime`. The server reads Google's metadata from its issuer, the setting `--google-issuer`, at the first sign-in start that reaches it.

parameters.name: return_to
parameters.description: The page of the web URL to return to once signed in: a path such as `/settings?tab=devices`, or its full address. Anything else, such as another site's address or the public URL's, returns to `/` of the web URL.

Location.description: Google's authorization endpoint with the client ID, the redirect URI `<web URL>/auth/google/callback`, `response_type=code`, the scopes `openid email`, `state`, `nonce`, `code_challenge` and `code_challenge_method=S256`.

Set-Cookie.description: The cookie that binds `state` to this browser: `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Secure` under an https web URL, for the callback's path only.

404.description: Google sign-in is off: the server has no Google settings.

502.description: Google is unreachable, or its metadata or keys are malformed.

get.description: Opened by the browser on its way back from Google. Checks `state` against the browser's cookie, exchanges `code` with the client ID and secret and the sign-in's PKCE verifier, and checks the ID token as OpenID Connect Core 1.0, §3.1.3.7, says, with this sign-in's `nonce`. The account is bound to its Google sign-in method, Google's issuer and the ID token's `sub`, never to the email. The first sign-in creates the account, its username made from the email's local part; later ones reach the account that holds that method, also after the email changes. While the server's sign-up is closed, a first sign-in creates an account for an email on the server's list whose `email_verified` is true, for an ID token whose `hd`, the Google Workspace or Cloud organization, is on its domain list, or through `PUT /auth/device/invite`; the email's domain does not count. Lists compare without case. Keeps no email, ID token or Google token. For a link, started by `POST /auth/google/link`, it adds the Google sign-in method to the account of the web session that started the link instead of signing in.

parameters.name: error

Or a refused sign-up: the server's sign-up is closed and the person, who has no account, is on none of its lists and has no usable invite proof on the device authorization; the page names the problem type `https://skald.so/problems/sign-up-closed`, and nothing is created. A sign-in from the verification page with a user code refuses that code too: its polls answer `sign_up_closed`.

404.description: Google sign-in is off: the server has no Google settings.

409.description: A link that links nothing: another account has this Google sign-in method. Accounts never merge or move a method.

500.description: No one is signed in, or nothing is linked: the database failed.

502.description: No one is signed in, or nothing is linked: Google failed, is unreachable or refused the client ID and secret.

post.summary: Start a link of a Google sign-in method
post.description: Starts a link as `POST /auth/github/link` does, with Google: sends the browser to Google as `GET /auth/google` does, with `prompt=select_account`, so that the person chooses the Google account; Google comes back through `GET /auth/google/callback`.

The request has no session; it signs a challenge from `POST /devices/{device}/challenge` and sends the device's complete certificate, which the server first stores if it holds none, as `PUT /devices/{device}/cert` does and within the devices limit. The session has no sign-in method; the server takes it as any device session and lists it with its device. It ends when its device is revoked, when it signs out, when a web session ends it, and when the device gets another session so.

post.description: A new `client` device that has no session opens a run of CPace keyed by its link code (docs/protocol/membership.md, "Link code"); the server relays it and never sees the code. The request names the device, which holds no certificate, is on no deleted account and may be registered on no account yet, and replaces that device's open run, whose messages are then refused. The server picks the run's pairing, which the device's hello binds and the person enters on the issuing device with the code, and gives it with the run's token for its messages; the hello follows as the run's first message, `POST /links/messages`. The run is no account's until a session enters its pairing, `POST /account/links/pairing`: no account's latest hello gives it, and its device is given as waiting only once it registers on an account. It ends as a run of `POST /account/links` does, and once the account its device registered on is deleted. The request has no session.

While idle, the stream sends a comment line at the interval of the server setting `--sse-keep-alive`. It ends when its session or service token ends or its device is revoked. A service token needs the `receive` permission, and gets notices of its space only and no `link-notice`. The device sends and acks with `POST /mailbox/send` and `POST /mailbox/ack`.

get.description: Opens a WebSocket (RFC 6455) after checking the protocol version the request states, as docs/protocol/README.md, "Server answers", says. Its first frame, `auth`, proves the connection's device on a challenge of `POST /session/challenge` (docs/protocol/delivery.md, "Connecting"); a connection without a valid proof is closed as "Connecting" there says. The server then answers each `send` with `stored` or `send-refused` ("Send" there) and, from the connection's first `sync`, sends its device's mailbox ("Mailbox" there). Once the server stores a roster revision, it sends `space-notice` on each connection of a device of an account the revision lists, and once a run of a device opens, `link-notice` on each connection of a device session of its account ("Frames" there). A connection on a service token's challenge sends only with the token's `send` permission, in its channels, gets notices of its space only, and gets nothing of its mailbox, its `sync` and `ack` ignored, without its `receive` permission.

last_used_at.description: The token's last request, to the minute: a request records its use only when the last one is a minute old or more. `null` before its first.

ServiceTokenId.description: A service token's ID: random, it reveals nothing of the token's value.

token.description: The run's token, for its messages: `Authorization: Bearer <token>` at `GET` and `POST /links/messages`, until the run ends. It is no session. The server keeps only its SHA-256.

device.description: The new device: with no certificate, registered on any account or none.

github_login.description: The GitHub login of the account's GitHub sign-in method as of its latest sign-in, for display; only while the account has one.

sign_in_method.description: The provider a web session signed in with; only for a web session.

web.description: The server's web URL, an origin, which invite links start with (docs/protocol/membership.md, "Invite"); absent on a server without sign-in.

SessionId.description: A session's ID: random, it reveals nothing of the session's token.

SignInMethod.description: A sign-in method: a provider and the subject it gives the person, which the server does not show.

linked_at.description: When the method was linked, or the account created with it.

github_login.description: A GitHub method's GitHub login as of its latest sign-in, for display; only for GitHub.

current.description: Whether the request's web session signed in with this method; `false` for a device session.

SignInMethodId.description: A sign-in method's ID: random, it reveals nothing of the method's subject.

SignInProvider.description: The sign-in provider: GitHub, Google, or the corporate OpenID Connect issuer.

providers.description: The providers the server has settings for, each once.

sign_up.description: `open`: a first sign-in creates an account. `closed`: a first sign-in creates an account for verified identities from the configured corporate issuer, listed identities, or identities with a usable device sign-up invite.

privacy_policy_url.description: The address of the server's privacy policy, the server setting `--privacy-policy-url`, which its sign-in pages link. Absent without the setting.

revocations.description: The stored revocations of the listed devices' accounts, each as the server got it, once.

records.description: The account record of each of those accounts that has one, as its first device sent it, once; an account whose master key came before account records has none.

deleted.description: The IDs of those accounts that are deleted, once each: the server's word; absent when none is. Their devices, certificates and revocations are still given.

SpaceId.description: A space's ID: a UUIDv7 in the lowercase hyphenated form (docs/protocol/README.md, "Identifiers").

SpaceName.description: A space's name: a valid `name` (docs/protocol/README.md, "Agent address"), unique on the server.

SpaceUsage.description: A space's messages this month and service agents, with its limits. When `plan` is present, the limits describe plan allowances, including those for members, devices and attachments. The server enforces limits from its settings.

members.description: The plan allowance for space members. Team has no member limit.

devices_per_member.description: The plan allowance for devices per space member.

monthly_messages.description: The space's messages this calendar month in UTC. Each message counts once regardless of its envelopes. Handshake messages are excluded. With plans off, the limit comes from `--monthly-messages-limit`.

message_size.description: The message text size allowance in bytes. With plans off, it is the envelope payload limit from `--message-size-limit`.

attachment_size.description: The plan allowance for attachment size in bytes.

mailbox_retention.description: Undelivered message retention in seconds. With plans off, the limit comes from `--mailbox-retention`.

history_retention.description: Channel history retention in seconds. With plans off, the limit comes from `--history-retention`.

service_agents.description: Service agent entries in the space's latest revision. Before the first revision the count is zero. With plans off, the limit comes from `--service-agents-limit`.

SupportedVersions.description: The protocol versions the server accepts, ascending.

Task.description: A task as the server gives it (docs/protocol/queues.md, "Task states").

queued_task.description: The `queued-task` as its device uploaded it, in base64url without padding (RFC 4648, §5).

progress.description: Of a `claimed` task, its holder's last extend; none before it.

claim.description: Its last claim, if it had one.

TaskId.description: A task's ID (`task`), issued by its sending device, in the lowercase hyphenated form (docs/protocol/README.md, "Identifiers").

UsageCount.description: A count and its limit; `limit` is absent while no limit applies.

UsageLimit.description: A limit; `limit` is absent while no limit applies.

Username.description: An account's username: a `name` of an agent address (docs/protocol/README.md, "Agent address"), unique on the server; `skald`, `admin`, `support` and `root` are reserved.

invite.description: The invite the acceptance is of, as the server got it.

acceptance.description: The acceptance as the server got it.

devices.description: The devices of the acceptance's account, each with its certificate as the device sent it, or `null` while it has none.

revocations.description: The stored revocations of the acceptance's account, each as the server got it, once.

kind.description: The kind the device registered with.

name.description: The name the device registered with.
